title: Per-vector slab pricing prototype and enterprise QSA alignment for embeddings + rerank
creator: Lena Thompson
description:
Summary:
We need a pragmatic pricing prototype that moves from a simple per-call embedding price to a per-vector unit economy with explicit batch/volume slabs and enterprise contract language that satisfies standard security questionnaires (QSA). The goal is to (1) reduce churn from unpredictable per-call spikes, (2) give enterprise buyers cost predictability for large reranking jobs, and (3) preserve unit economics for Redwood by keeping a lower bound on per-vector revenue after batching effects.

Hypothesis:
- Charging per-vector (1 vector = 1 embedding vector output) with tiered volume discounts will increase adoption for high-throughput reranking customers and will capture more upstream spend that today gets hidden in custom contracts.
- Reasonable slab thresholds + a handshake floor price prevents margin erosion when customers apply extreme batching and KV-cache techniques.

Proposed pricing prototype (short):
- Base SKU: embeddings.vector.unit priced at $0.00015 / vector for first 1M vectors / month.
- Slab discounts: 1M-10M => 10% off, 10M-100M => 25% off, 100M+ => 40% off. Discounts apply to vectors consumed beyond slab thresholds (marginal pricing).
- Batch Accelerator Credit: for requests that include explicit batch param in API (batch_size > 1) we apply a lightweight batching multiplier that reduces unit price by up to additional 5% for batch_size > 32, subject to abuse checks.
- Rerank add-on: reranking call counts as N vectors where N = input_candidates * output_vectors; documentation will recommend streaming tools for very large candidate sets to avoid unbounded bills.
- Contract/Enterprise: allow custom committed-volume discounts with minimums and true-up monthly. Security questionnaire (QSA) acceptance criteria included in contract appendix.

Trade-offs discussed:
- Per-vector pricing is easier to reason about for customers, but we need to mitigate arbitrage where customers craft unnatural requests to inflate vector efficiency. We will use soft caps + abuse monitoring (ENG-2899).
- Batch discounts encourage efficient client-side batching vs naive single-row calls; however, too aggressive discounts reduce revenue for small but high-value customers. Hence slab thresholds are conservative.

Data & analytics plan:
- Instrument billing to record: vectors_emitted, batch_size, deduped_vectors, rerank_candidates, per-request latency.
- Dashboard KPIs: MRR by slab, average unit price realized, expected CPU/GPU cost per 1M vectors, churn rate for top 50 customers, and contract true-up deltas. Dashboard prototype: https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/embeddings/pricing-telemetry (internal).

Technical implementation notes:
- Billing: map embeddings.vector.unit to existing metered billing path in Stripe. Metered unit = vectors_emitted (rounded up). Avoid fractional units for clarity.
- API: add header "X-Vector-Count" in debug responses to enable customers to reconcile usage.
- Guardrails: ENG to implement abuse detection rules (dependent ENG-2714) and server-side batch multiplier validation (ENG-2899).

QSA / Contract workstream:
- Security appendix draft linked in Confluence: https://company.drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3cQSA-embeddings (internal doc). It enumerates data flow, retention, encryption, and audit logs for embeddings vectors.
- Required answers for customers' security questionnaires (SOC2/ISO-like) prepared in the vendor questionnaire sheet: https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1QSA-Embeddings-Responses. Contract language proposed to legal for review: gs://redwood-legal/contracts/embeddings-slab-2026.docx (placeholder link).

Rollout & experiment plan:
- Week 1 (canary): small-sample A/B test on hosted API for all new sign-ups with <10k vectors/month (5% traffic) to measure adoption and billing behavior.
- Week 2-3: enable for 10 pilot enterprise customers under commercial negotiation; update CPQ to show slab-estimated TCO.
- Week 4: open opt-in for production customers; default for existing customers remains current billing unless they opt into the slab pricing with a signed contract amendment.

Acceptance criteria:
- Billing pipeline correctly records vectors_emitted and computes slab discounts in test env for 3 weeks with no data loss.
- Dashboard shows unit economics delta and revenue protection signals.
- Legal approves contract appendix and security answers; QSA fields signed off by Security.
- Two pilot enterprise customers sign contracts using slab model and billing reconciles to expected true-up within 10%.

Open questions / decisions needed:
1) Exact slab breakpoints — current proposal conservative; product + finance to confirm (suggested: move 100M -> 250M if finance prefers).
2) Batch Accelerator logic: linear multiplier or discrete thresholds? Engineering preference (ENG-2899) leans discrete.
3) Rerank counting model for streaming pipelines (we need to finalize how streaming partial candidates are charged).

Next steps:
- Design + Finance alignment meeting (Priya, Marco, Asha) scheduled 2026-02-24.
- ENG tickets ENG-2714 (metering schema) and ENG-2899 (abuse/batching validation) to be prioritized in Cycle 2026-W10.
- Legal to deliver draft contract appendix by 2026-03-01.
